title: Phonon Scharnhorst effect: Acoustic analogue of the vacuum-fluctuation-boosted speed of light
abstract: The Scharnhorst effect in quantum electrodynamics predicts a superluminal velocity shift $δc>0$ at low photon frequencies due to vacuum fluctuations between two mirrors. Although theoretically robust (no causality violation), the effect is extraordinarily small ($δc/c\approx 10^{-32}$ for mirrors $1\,μ{\rm m}$ apart) and outside current experimental reach. Here we propose a condensed matter analogue, replacing the photons in the electromagnetic vacuum by phonon excitations of a Bose-Einstein condensate. In an idealized geometry, the two-dimensional surface of a cylinder (circumference $L$) at zero temperature, the axial speed of sound is increased due to zero-point fluctuations of the condensate by $δc/c\simeq 5\times 10^{-3}\,\tilde{g}$ at $L\simeq 2\,ξ$, to first order in the dimensionless interaction constant $\tilde{g}\simeq 10^{-1}$ of the Bose gas of healing length $ξ\simeq 1\,μ{\rm m}$. This is 28 orders of magnitude larger than the photonic effect, basically because phonons have a self-interaction while photons only interact via massive electrons. We discuss the prospects for observation of the acoustic Scharnhorst effect, the main restriction being the low-temperature requirement.
summary: This theoretical paper adapts the concept of the Scharnhorst effect, which predicts superluminal speed shifts from vacuum fluctuations, to the context of Bose-Einstein condensates. By modeling phonons in a BEC confined to a cylinder, the authors calculate a predicted speed-of-sound shift that is vastly larger than the QED prediction. The methodology relies on advanced many-body techniques applied to quasi-2D quantum gases.
main_problem: The paper proposes a condensed matter analogue to the Scharnhorst effect, predicting a superluminal velocity shift in the speed of sound of a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) due to zero-point vacuum fluctuations.
main_result: The predicted relative velocity shift ($\delta c/c_0$) is significantly larger (by 28 orders of magnitude) than the analogous effect in QED, making it a potentially observable phenomenon in BECs.
method: The authors use Bogoliubov theory and the Abel-Plana formula to calculate the vacuum energy density contribution from zero-point fluctuations in a quasi-2D geometry.
model_or_system: The system is a dilute Bose gas confined to the surface of a cylinder, modeled using the Gross-Pitaevskii theory. The analysis involves geometric renormalization to derive an effective 2D coupling constant.
key_observables: The relative velocity shift ($\delta c/c_0$) of the phonon spectrum, which appears as a common displacement across the frequency ladder ($\omega_j = \pi j c/L_{ax}$).
important_parameters: Healing length ($\xi$), cylinder circumference ($L$), dimensionless interaction constant ($	ilde{g}$), and the ratio $L/\xi$.
main_assumptions: The primary calculation assumes an idealized, strictly 2D Bose gas geometry, and the results are derived for zero temperature, though finite temperature corrections are discussed.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the scaling functions $F(\ell)$ and $G(\ell)$ that determine the energy and sound velocity dependence on the ratio $\ell = L/\xi$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the QED analogue, then modeling the BEC system on a cylinder, deriving the effective 2D Hamiltonian via renormalization, and finally calculating the velocity shift using fluctuation theory and addressing geometric and thermal corrections.
why_interesting: This work directly connects fundamental concepts from quantum electrodynamics (vacuum fluctuations) to controllable, highly tunable systems like BECs, providing a concrete, large-scale analogue for experimental investigation in AMO physics.
